title: Rashidun Caliphate
capsule: The Rashidun Caliphate was the early Islamic state governed by the first four caliphs — Abu Bakr (632–634), Umar ibn al-Khattab (634–644), Uthman ibn Affan (644–656), and Ali ibn Abi Talib (656–661) — attested here from 633 to 665. Under Umar the caliphate launched its most dramatic expansions: Arab armies defeated the Sasanian Empire at al-Qadisiyyah (636) and Nihavand (642), conquered Byzantine Syria at Yarmouk (636), and occupied Egypt by 642. Uthman's assassination in 656 triggered the First Fitna, the civil war between Ali and Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan that ended with Ali's murder in 661 and Muawiyah's founding of the Umayyad Caliphate, absorbing the Rashidun state.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Rashidun territorial control is documented in early Islamic historical sources (al-Tabari, al-Baladhuri) and is reasonably reliable for core conquered provinces; precise frontier lines in Persia and North Africa during the conquest phase are approximations based on campaign narratives.
